executive_summary: Moosewave Campaigns has solid table-stakes plus differentiators competitors lack: collaborative cursors, per-campaign feedback threads, sandbox lifecycle, fingerprint-gated approvals, dynamic-content regions, voice-drift banner, Inbox Reality predictor, STO. Three strongest 2026 themes: (1) Reply-as-channel — Litmus Live 2026 frames replies as cleanest engagement signal, Moosewave can extend feedback surfaces into inbound classification; (2) Per-recipient send-time + bandit allocation layered on existing SendTimeOptBanner; (3) Bot-stripped Human metrics + per-campaign timeseries — today’s report is point-in-time and Apple MPP makes raw opens noise. specs.title: Frequency cap rules + recipient-local quiet hours at queue-fill
specs.overview: Adds two send-time guardrails to /queue: (a) tenant-level frequency_cap_rules (e.g. max 3/24h) evaluated against a new subscriber_send_log, and (b) per-recipient quiet hours that suppress sends when the recipient's local clock (subscribers.timezone, fallback tenant TZ) falls inside the configured window. Both run inside queueCampaignCore after suppression/holdout/A-B, surface skip/defer counters in queueResponse + CampaignReport, and are tenant-opt-in (empty rules + null window = pass-through). Closes parity with Customer.io's global frequency caps and per-recipient quiet hours.
specs.user_flow: 1. Admin opens Settings → Sending settings, scrolls to a new "Frequency caps" card, clicks Add rule, enters "Max 3 / 24h", saves. 2. In the existing Quiet hours card, admin toggles "Use recipient local time" and confirms 22:00–08:00. 3. Operator queues a campaign. queueCampaignCore runs audience → suppression → holdout → A/B, then evaluates frequency caps (subscriber_send_log per email) and per-recipient quiet hours (subscriber.timezone). 4. Response now carries recipients_queued, recipients_skipped_frequency_cap, recipients_deferred_quiet_hours plus a per-rule breakdown. 5. The slideover Performance card renders two new chips below the stat tiles; clicking the cap chip opens a modal of rule-by-rule skip counts. 6. Audit log records one campaign.frequency_filtered event per send.

open_questions: V1 SKIP-only or SKIP+DEFER for quiet hours? Customer.io defers (auto-requeues when the window closes); this spec ships skip-only and notes defer-and-requeue as V2 — confirm acceptable for the launch claim.

Should frequency caps count `pending` recipient rows or only `sent` ones? Counting pending prevents double-queue races but causes same-hour resend bugs if the first campaign fails. Spec assumes count of `sent` rows only — confirm.

Per-channel caps (email vs SMS vs push) like Customer.io's matrix, or one global cap covering all channels? Spec assumes one cap; the sms package already has its own quiet_hours so the new table only governs email.

Hard floor for system/transactional mail (e.g. password resets must always go regardless of cap)? Likely yes — gate on campaigns.is_transactional if it exists, otherwise add a bypass_frequency_caps boolean to the campaigns row.

subscriber_send_log retention: indefinite, 90 days, or driven by retention_policies (migration 0238)? Spec leaves the table un-rotated; for tenants sending 1M+/day the row count explodes — recommend wiring into the existing retention sweep package.

specs.title: Subject Lab: confidence-scored variants with one-click bandit handoff

A "Run top 3 as bandit A/B" button hands top-3 by lower-CI bound into the existing /campaigns/ab-test flow with delivery_settings.ab_test.bandit=true so G4's dispatcher picks them up.
